# Hill numbers {#sec-hill}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}
$$
    ^q D = \left( \sum_{i = 1}^S p_i^q \right)^{\frac{1}{1-q}}
$${#eq-hill}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

### Hill numbers (q = 0, 1, 2) with dune data

Using the classic `dune` dataset from the `vegan` package:

```{r}
library(vegan)
data(dune)

# Calculate Hill numbers for each site
# q = 0: Species richness (number of species)
hill_q0 <- specnumber(dune)

# q = 1: Exponential of Shannon entropy (exp(H))
# Related to Shannon index but easier to interpret
shannon <- diversity(dune, index = "shannon")
hill_q1 <- exp(shannon)

# q = 2: Inverse Simpson index (1/lambda)
# Related to Simpson index
hill_q2 <- diversity(dune, index = "invsimpson")

# Combine into a table
hill_numbers <- data.frame(
  Site = rownames(dune),
  q0_Richness = hill_q0,
  q1_Shannon = round(hill_q1, 2),
  q2_Simpson = round(hill_q2, 2)
)

head(hill_numbers)
```

### Interpretation of Hill numbers

```{r}
# For a specific site, compare the three Hill numbers
site_1 <- hill_numbers[1, ]
cat("Site 1 Hill Numbers:\n")
cat("q=0 (Richness):", site_1$q0_Richness, "- actual number of species\n")
cat("q=1 (Shannon):", site_1$q1_Shannon, "- effective number of equally-common species\n")
cat("q=2 (Simpson):", site_1$q2_Simpson, "- effective number weighted by dominants\n")
cat("\nRatio q0/q2:", round(site_1$q0_Richness / site_1$q2_Simpson, 2), 
    "- higher = more even distribution\n")
```

### Select three representative sites

```{r}
# Select sites with different richness and evenness patterns
site_indices <- c(1, 10, 20)  # Low, medium, high richness
representative_sites <- dune[site_indices, ]

# Extract their Hill numbers
rep_hills <- hill_numbers[site_indices, ]
rep_hills
```

### Rarefaction curves (interpolation)

```{r}
# Create rarefaction curves for the three sites
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))

for(i in seq_along(site_indices)) {
  site_data <- representative_sites[i, ]
  
  # Rarefaction curve (interpolation)
  rare <- rarefy(site_data, sample = 1:sum(site_data))
  
  plot(1:sum(site_data), rare,
       type = "l", lwd = 2, col = "steelblue",
       main = paste("Site", site_indices[i]),
       xlab = "Number of Individuals",
       ylab = "Number of Species",
       ylim = c(1, max(rep_hills$q0_Richness)))
  
  # Add a point at the observed richness
  points(sum(site_data), rep_hills$q0_Richness[i], 
         pch = 16, col = "red", cex = 2)
  
  # Add reference line
  abline(h = rep_hills$q0_Richness[i], lty = 2, col = "gray")
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

### Species accumulation curves (interpolation)

```{r}
# Accumulation curves for the three representative sites
par(mfrow = c(1, 3))

for(i in seq_along(site_indices)) {
  site_data <- representative_sites[i, ]
  
  # Get non-zero species (those actually present)
  sp_present <- site_data[site_data > 0]
  
  # Create a simple accumulation by adding species one at a time
  n_species <- length(sp_present)
  accumulated <- cumsum(rep(1, n_species))
  
  plot(1:n_species, accumulated,
       type = "s", lwd = 2, col = "darkgreen",
       main = paste("Site", site_indices[i]),
       xlab = "Species (ordered by abundance)",
       ylab = "Cumulative Number of Species",
       ylim = c(1, max(rep_hills$q0_Richness)))
  
  # Add final richness point
  points(n_species, rep_hills$q0_Richness[i],
         pch = 16, col = "red", cex = 2)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

### Extrapolation using Chao2

```{r}
# Estimate species richness using Chao2 estimator
# (This estimates the true richness if sampling was complete)

par(mfrow = c(1, 3))

for(i in seq_along(site_indices)) {
  site_data <- representative_sites[i, ]
  
  # Calculate Chao2 estimate
  # Requires presence/absence data
  site_pa <- ifelse(site_data > 0, 1, 0)
  
  # Chao2 formula: S_obs + (f1^2 / (2*f2))
  # where f1 = number of singletons, f2 = number of doubletons
  observed_richness <- sum(site_pa)
  
  # Get abundance classes
  f1 <- sum(site_data == 1)  # Singletons (appear once)
  f2 <- sum(site_data == 2)  # Doubletons (appear twice)
  
  # Chao2 estimator
  if(f2 > 0) {
    chao2 <- observed_richness + (f1^2) / (2 * f2)
  } else {
    chao2 <- observed_richness + (f1 * (f1 - 1)) / (2 * (f2 + 1))
  }
  
  # Plot observed vs estimated richness
  x_vals <- c(0, 1, 1.5)
  y_vals <- c(observed_richness, observed_richness, chao2)
  
  plot(x_vals, y_vals, type = "o", lwd = 2, pch = c(16, 16, 17),
       col = c("steelblue", "steelblue", "red"),
       main = paste("Site", site_indices[i]),
       xlab = "",
       ylab = "Number of Species",
       ylim = c(0, chao2 * 1.3),
       xlim = c(-0.2, 1.7))
  
  # Add segments for extrapolation
  segments(1, observed_richness, 1.5, chao2, 
           lty = 2, col = "red", lwd = 1.5)
  
  # Labels
  text(x_vals, y_vals, 
       labels = c("Observed", "Observed", paste("Chao2:", round(chao2, 1))),
       pos = c(2, 2, 4), cex = 0.8)
  
  axis(1, at = c(0, 1, 1.5), 
       labels = c("", "Observed", "Extrapolated"), cex.axis = 0.7)
}

par(mfrow = c(1, 1))
```

### Compare Hill numbers across the three sites

```{r}
# Visualize the relationship between Hill numbers
plot(rep_hills$q0_Richness, rep_hills$q2_Simpson,
     pch = 16, col = "steelblue", cex = 2,
     main = "Hill Number q=0 vs q=2",
     xlab = "q=0 (Richness)",
     ylab = "q=2 (Inverse Simpson)",
     xlim = c(0, max(rep_hills$q0_Richness) * 1.1),
     ylim = c(0, max(rep_hills$q0_Richness) * 1.1))

# Add diagonal line (perfect evenness: q2 = q0)
abline(0, 1, lty = 2, col = "gray", lwd = 1)

# Add labels
text(rep_hills$q0_Richness, rep_hills$q2_Simpson,
     labels = paste("Site", site_indices),
     pos = 3, cex = 0.8)

# Add legend
legend("bottomright", legend = "Line: q0 = q2 (perfect evenness)",
       lty = 2, col = "gray", cex = 0.8)
```

### Summary table

```{r}
# Create a comprehensive summary
summary_table <- data.frame(
  Site = paste("Site", site_indices),
  Richness_q0 = rep_hills$q0_Richness,
  Shannon_q1 = rep_hills$q1_Shannon,
  Simpson_q2 = rep_hills$q2_Simpson,
  Evenness = round(rep_hills$q2_Simpson / rep_hills$q0_Richness, 3)
)

print(summary_table)

cat("\nInterpretation:\n")
cat("- q=0 increases with richness only\n")
cat("- q=1 balances richness and evenness\n")
cat("- q=2 is dominated by most abundant species\n")
cat("- Evenness = q2/q0: higher = more even distribution\n")
```
